issue: Does the no-proximate-cause rule that applies to the drug-penalty enhancement in 21 U.S.C. § 841(b) extend beyond that drug-sentencing context to other federal statutes with 'results from' language?

sides.position: The § 841(b) no-proximate-cause rule does not extend to other statutes. It is an exception limited to drug-sentencing factors, and courts should not apply it to a different statute such as a human smuggling provision.
cases: United States v. Pineda-Doval, 614 F.3d 1019, 1026–28 (9th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Covington, No. 25-4282 (4th Cir. July 2, 2026)

sides.position: The § 841(b) no-proximate-cause rule extends to other statutes, including a healthcare fraud statute.
cases: United States v. Webb, 655 F.3d 1238, 1255–56 (11th Cir. 2011)

quote: What is more, our sister circuits are divided about whether (and if so, when) Section 841(b)’s no-proximate-cause rule extends beyond that provision’s specific context.
cite: United States v. Shronda Covington, No. 25-4282 (4th Cir. 2026)
